name: Nerv
prior: No plugin, app or Eurorack module with an Izhikevich (or FitzHugh-Nagumo / Hodgkin-Huxley) neuron as its audio oscillator was found (searches: 'Izhikevich spiking neuron audio oscillator synthesizer', 'FitzHugh-Nagumo OR Hodgkin-Huxley neuron oscillator synthesizer plugin', 'neuron oscillator Eurorack'). Closest: Snyder, Bhatia, Mulshine, 'Neuron-modeled Audio Synthesis: Nonlinear Sound and Control', NIME 2018 - a software instrument whose sound generation is a biological neuron model, with a laptop-orchestra piece (VS: nime.org/proc/nime2018_snyderb; full text blocked by the proxy, model type unverified - A: HH/FHN class); Miranda and Matthias 2005 'Granular sampling using a pulse-coupled network of spiking neurons' and McCracken/Matthias/Miranda 2011 'Neurogranular synthesis' - spiking networks trigger grains at event rate, not an audio oscillator (VS: springerprofessional.de/granular-sampling-using-a-pulse-coupled-network-of-spiking-neuro/2663766; evomusart-index.dei.uc.pt/authors/385); Miranda 'Music neurotechnology for sound synthesis' Leonardo 2009 and in-vitro neuron instruments, CellF (VS: researchportal.plymouth.ac.uk; lasalle.edu.sg cellf). Hardware: Nonlinearcircuits Dual Neuron / Difference Rectifier - analog Mueller-type threshold neuron, rectifies the input and adds pulses when the threshold is crossed, audio-rate capable, DIY only; no excitable ODE, no bursting (VS: modulargrid.net/e/nonlinearcircuits-dual-neuron-diff-rect-papernoise-panel). Name-only: Audio Damage ADM12 Neuron (FM drum, discontinued; VS: modulargrid.net/e/audio-damage-adm12-neuron), ARC Artificial Neural Network (threshold logic; VS: synthtopia.com 2017/11/18), IRCAM Neurorack (AI; VS: synthtopia.com 2022/01/08). Tiny Tapeout tt06/334 'Izhikevich Neuron' is an ASIC demo, not audio (VS: tinytapeout.com/chips/tt06/334). Rare: the neuron-as-sound idea exists in academia and one analog module, the Izhikevich oscillator with a regime path and cross-voice coupling in a playable instrument does not.
costNotes: Worklet only (sample-level ODE with reset, feedback inside the block). Measured (M: sim/eng_min5.js and eng_nrv_cost2.js, Node 22 x64 on a shared Xeon, min of 5 runs, numbers noisy +-50 %): Euler 2 substeps + sinus entrainment drive + DC block + softclip + 2 complex resonators = 57 ns/sample = 0.47 Nebel units; 1 substep 46 ns = 0.38; without resonators 51 ns = 0.42 (the ODE + reset + drive dominate, the resonators are cheap). The idea's '12 flops ~ 20 ns' is 2-3x optimistic in JS: the per-sample branch on v >= 30, the table read for the drive and the DC block cost as much as the ODE. Add worklet node 0.06 + 3 params (detune, freq, hoehe) 0.09 -> ~0.6 at level 1; level 3 (2 neurons coupled + 4 resonators) ~1.0 (the 2-neuron row measured 31 ns is a JIT artefact of the polymorphic bench, do not trust it; count 2x the ODE). Phone x1.0-1.5 (R: webaudio.md section 4). Still one of the cheaper engines - three fingers + lane = 2.4 units. Calibration table (f_model over a 32-point regime grid) is an offline simulation of ~0.5 model-seconds per point = ~2 ms each in the module scope, done once.
soundHeld: Pitch is exact and linear in the time scale s: spike rate = 22.3 Hz x s at I = 10 (M: s = 1 -> 23 Hz, 8 -> 178, 32 -> 692 Hz), so f = s * f_model(I, a, b, c, d) and setF/Bebung on s are clean; 2 Euler substeps stay finite up to s = 32 (dt_model 0.33 ms) - above ~700 Hz the note must come from a higher I (fast regime) rather than a larger s, so the top octave is timbre-locked to 'fast spiking' - cap the range at ~800 Hz. Entrainment works better than the idea assumes: a sinusoidal drive of 2 (20 % of I) at 170-200 Hz pulls the free 178-Hz neuron to within 1 Hz of the drive (M: 170 -> 171, 190 -> 191, 200 -> 201), i.e. a lock window of at least +-10 %, and 400 Hz gives a 2:1 lock; I-noise of 20-60 % of I leaves the mean rate at 178 Hz (only ISI jitter) - pitch is robust, 'Rauschen' is a free liveliness knob. The regime path is NOT a smooth timbre slider: interpolating (c, d) from (-65, 8) to (-50, 2) at fixed s gives burst-rate steps 178 -> 200 -> 234 -> 252 -> 172 -> 184 -> 304 -> 165 -> 262 Hz (M: period-adding bifurcations; spikes per burst 1 -> 2 -> 3 ...), so the perceived fundamental jumps by fifths and octaves along Hoehe unless s is re-calibrated per y against the measured burst period, and even then the timbre steps like registers. Regular regime after the DC block is a relaxation ramp + spike = saw with a click ('saegenah', as the idea admits); the identity is the bursting band (y 0.3-0.9: pitched growl with a sub-period), the resonators, the coupling. Cross-voice coupling via module-scope state is feasible (one thread, one module), but per-block means a 2.7-ms = s x 2.7 = 21 model-ms delay at s = 8: not a gap junction, a slow current injection - 'who pulls whom' happens as drift of rate/burstiness over tens of ms, and g must stay small or coupled chord members detune beyond the +-10 % lock window.
soundBurst: A Puls hit as current pulse gives an instant volley (first spike within one model-ms = 0.1 ms audio) into the resonators: a tight 'zap' with pitch, distinct from Membran/Glocke, and the volley raises the shared field so holding Nerv voices twitch on every hit - cheap and audibly causal. In the regular regime a 50-ms hit is a thin saw blip; Puls presets must sit in bursting/chattering with resonators. Rebound ('Nachschlag') is a real Izhikevich property but only for rebound-spike parameters (a 0.03, b 0.25, c -60, d 4 - A: Izhikevich 2004 figure), so it is a regime, not a global knob: implement release as I -> negative for 20-50 model-ms in that regime only; elsewhere release is just the envelope.
failureModes: Hoehe is a staircase, not a slider: period-adding bifurcations along the regime path jump the fundamental by fifths/octaves (M); needs a y-indexed calibration of s plus the entrainment drive, and UI wording as registers (Ticken / Ton / Salven)
Regular regime = saw with click; without the resonator body and bursting defaults it is 'Nebel with a tick'
Cost ~0.6 not 0.32: the ODE branch, drive table and DC block cost as much as the 12 flops (M)
Range: above ~700 Hz s > 32 destabilises Euler; must switch to high-I fast regimes -> timbre tied to pitch; cap at 800 Hz
Block-wise coupling (21 model-ms delay at s = 8) is not a gap junction; strong g detunes coupled voices out of the lock window
Rebound exists only in a specific (a, b, c, d) corner - cannot be a free parameter
Worklet thread move (R: webaudio.md section 2) and exceptions in process() silence the voice for good (section 3) - clamp v, u every block
Gestik Bebung on s is clean, but Hoehe offsets through the regime path trigger the staircase audibly - smooth y with 40 ms
verdict: Rare: neuron-model synthesis exists in academia (Snyder et al. NIME 2018, Miranda's neurogranular work) and as an analog threshold module (Nonlinearcircuits Dual Neuron), but no playable Izhikevich audio oscillator with a regime path and coupled voices was found. Worklet, measured ~0.47 units for the core and ~0.6 with node and params (twice the idea's figure, still cheap), ~1.0 at level 3. The simulation confirms the good parts - pitch linear in s, entrainment locks within +-10 %, noise does not detune - and exposes the main flaw: the regime path is a staircase of period-adding jumps (burst rate 252 -> 172 Hz between y 0.5 and 0.6), so Hoehe needs a per-y calibration table and should be presented as registers; the regular regime is a saw with a click, the identity lives in bursting, the resonator body, the per-hit field twitch and the rebound corner. Build it, range 40-800 Hz, bursting as the default.
